page.overview:
What is Olathoë?

Olathoë is a fictional extra-dimensional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "Polaris".

Olathoë is a great fortified city of marble in the far northern kingdom of Lomar in the Dreamlands. It lies on the Plateau of Sarkis in a hollow between the mountains Noton and Kadiphonek. Olathoë faces external threats from a horde of ruthless conquerors known as the Inutos that appeared out of the unknown west. The city is also threatened by the gradual encroachment of a great advancing ice sheet that long ago displaced the Zobnarians, the ancestors of the Lomarians. (: "Polaris")

Olathoë's architecture makes extensive use of marble in its construction. The upper parts of the pillars are carved into the images of bearded men, and the public squares where people gather to converse contain many statues. As a city in a high northern latitude region, Olathoë experiences periods of continual daylight and darkness. (: "Polaris")

Olathoë is a repository for the grimoire known as the Pnakotic Manuscripts, as well as books that contain the wisdom of the Zobnarian Fathers. (: "Polaris")
